title: Is Miami still a tech hub?
summary: Is Miami still a tech hub? Pave data shows how hiring and pay changed after the crypto crash, and what it means for setting pay in a hot market.
body_markdown:
In the early days of remote work driven by COVID, Miami became a destination for tech talent almost overnight. While the weather is nothing to complain about, much of this was driven by the rise of the crypto industry. And it wasn’t just tech employees making the move; major investors like a16z opened Miami outposts.


Since 2021, the gap in pay between many markets in the US and the SF Bay Area has started to close. Miami stands out not just for how quickly the labor (and pay) market changed, but also the rise in pay over historical norms.


## Miami's boom unwound as crypto cooled


The story changed once we hit the end of 2023. As remote work shifted more toward hybrid models, or even full returns to office, pay outside the Bay Area started to normalize.


The end of 2023 also marked the end of a particularly rough patch for the crypto industry. A brief timeline:


- May 2022: MiamiCoin, hailed by Mayor Francis Suarez as an asset that could eventually “eliminate municipal taxes entirely”, has lost about[95% of its value](https://futurism.com/miami-crypto-imploded) .
- November 2022: FTX collapsed and declared[bankruptcy](https://www.cnbc.com/2022/11/11/sam-bankman-frieds-cryptocurrency-exchange-ftx-files-for-bankruptcy.html) .
- 2023: “Venture winter” kicked off.[Local venture capital inflows cratered](https://www.betaboom.com/magazine/article/miamis-crypto-revolution-a-global-destination) from a record $5.5 billion in 2022 down to just $400 million by mid-2023.


By 2024, a16z had[closed](https://techcrunch.com/2024/09/04/andreessen-horowitz-shutters-its-miami-office-after-two-years/) its Miami office. Over the course of 2024-2025, it became clear that many Web3 and tech companies that took advantage of Miami’s marketing and tax incentives[failed to deliver](https://www.bizjournals.com/southflorida/news/2025/01/16/miami-tech-startups-funding-business-covid.html) the thousands of physical local jobs they had promised.


## Miami hiring fell sharply in 2023

All of this, of course, impacts how companies in Miami are paying.


As we compare pay in Miami to other metro areas in the US, Miami is now clustering closer to cities like Dallas and Detroit—and drifting below historically higher paying cities like Washington DC and Los Angeles.


‍


## Ask what's behind a pay premium


The story of Miami shows how quickly technological and cultural changes can re-shape a labor market. But it also shows that just about any trend can reverse itself almost as fast.


For anyone setting pay in a hot market, the lesson is to ask what’s actually driving the premium. If it rests on a single industry or a short-lived incentive, plan for the possibility that it won’t last.[Pay premiums](https://www.pave.com/blog-posts/tech-ai-talent-premium) hold only as long as the jobs behind them do, and the market can move faster than your[pay bands](https://www.pave.com/blog-posts/compensation-bands-how-to-build-ones-that-last) . Make sure you’re using a data source that can keep pace and allow you to stay nimble.
